div.l: And thus with feyned flaterye / and Iapes
He made the ꝑpersoıı̄un/ and the peple his apys
But trewly to tellen / at laste
He was in chirche / a noble ecclesiastre
Wel covde he reden· / a lesson̄ or a story
For wel he wiste / whan that song was songe
But altherbest / he song an offertory
He muste p ̉reche / and weel a fyle his tonge
To wynne sylver· / as he wel covde
Therfor he song / the meryere and lowde
NOw have I tolde yow sothly / in a clause
Thastat tharray the noıı̄unber / and eek the cause
Why that assembled / was this companye
In southwerk / at this Ientil hostlerye
That hihte the Tabbard / faste bi the belle
But now is tyme / to yow for to telle
How that we bar vs / that Ilche nyht
Whan that we were / in that hosterye a lyht
And after wol I telle / of owr wiage
And al the remenānt / of owr pilgrymage
But first I pray yow / of yowr curtesye
That ye ne rette it nouht / my vylaynye
Though that I plenery / speke in this maateere
To telle yow here mater / and here cheere
Ne thouh I speke / here wordys ꝓpropirly
For this ye knowen / as wel as I ·
Who so shal tellen / a tale after a man
He mote reherse / as nyh as he can̄
Euerych worde yf it be in his charge
Al speke he neueyr / so rudly ne large
Or ell he mot tellyn his tale / vntrewe
Or feynyn thynges / or fyndyn wordys newe
He may nat sparee / al though he were his brothyr
